start.html:
Meep

Meep is a carefully assembled Ubuntu desktop environment for people who want a capable, creative, and developer-friendly computer without having to build every part of it themselves.

The installer will prepare the current Meep system for your computer, preserving the polished desktop experience while bringing together the tools needed for everyday work, development, media, and system administration.

Technologies:

  • Ubuntu and Cinnamon desktop
    with a familiar Linux workspace, desktop utilities, system settings, and a practical foundation for everyday computing.
  • Command-line foundations
    including APT, software repository support, Git, Git LFS, curl, wget, GnuPG, jq, nano, and tools for ZIP, GZIP, 7-Zip, and other archive formats.
  • Creative and office software
    including GIMP for image editing, Inkscape for vector graphics, LibreOffice for documents, VLC for media playback, SimpleScreenRecorder, and File Roller for archives.
  • Web browsing and communication
    with Google Chrome, Slack, Discord, Zoom, and additional desktop clients for collaboration, meetings, messaging, and daily web-based work.
  • Web server development
    with Apache, PHP-FPM, a broad PHP module set, Composer for dependency management, Symfony CLI, and Drush Launcher for PHP and Drupal workflows.
  • Databases and data services
    including MySQL client and server, PostgreSQL, Redis, Redis Server, and Memcached for relational data, caching, queues, and application development.
  • JavaScript and application tooling
    with Node.js, npm, Electron, ESLint, Sass, Nodemon, Heroku tooling, and developer utilities for building, testing, and running modern applications.
  • Multi-language development
    with Python and pip, Go, Java, Gradle, Maven, Ruby, Rake, Rustup, and Perl to support a wide range of programming languages and build systems.
  • Containers and virtual machines
    with Docker and Docker Compose for isolated services, QEMU for emulation, VirtualBox for desktop virtual machines, and tools for managing virtual disks.
  • Security, networking, and synchronization
    with UFW and Gufw firewall controls, rsync and rclone for file synchronization, GVFS backends for connected storage, and Meep performance services such as zram and managed temporary caches.
